title: Microsoft Teams: new sharing panel in meetings
summary: The briefing omits Microsoft's supplied rollout notice, which says the experience is enabled by default and includes Teams for the web. It treats published rollout timing and affected users as unknown and fails to explain the temporary individual opt-out.

claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting policies. 2. Select the policy that you want to edit. 3. Go to the Content sharing section.

claims.claim: Screen sharing mode is a per-user meeting-policy setting.
claims.quote: Screen sharing mode: This setting is a per-user policy. The setting controls whether a user can share a desktop and window in a Teams meeting.

claims.claim: The existing content-sharing controls described are per-user policy settings.
claims.quote: PowerPoint Live: This is a per-user policy. ... The Whiteboard setting for Teams meetings is a per-user setting. ... Shared notes: This setting is a per-user policy.

claims.claim: Meeting-policy values apply through the policy assigned to a user.
claims.quote: You can edit the settings in the global policy or create and assign one or more custom policies. Users get the global policy unless you create and assign a custom policy.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/meeting-policies-overview and clarify the assignment sentence: users receive the global policy automatically unless a custom policy is assigned; a separate manual assignment is not always necessary.

claims.claim: The cited content-sharing policy article lists no licence requirement for its content-sharing settings.
claims.quote: Searched: licence, license, licensing and prerequisites in the full fetched article https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/meeting-policies-content-sharing. No licence requirement is listed there; this does not establish licensing for the redesigned panel.

claims.where: Scope: second paragraph; summary; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published which users are in scope for the new sharing-panel experience.
claims.quote: Who is affected: - All Teams work and school users joining meetings ... Teams for Windows desktop ... Teams for Mac desktop ... Teams for the web
claims.fix: State that MC1317197 covers all Teams work and school users joining meetings on Windows desktop, Mac desktop and the web; it excludes Teams consumer, iOS, Android, Teams Rooms and Linux. Preserve the narrower roadmap platform list as a separately attributed record fact. When adding web coverage, include Learn's caveat that Single application behaves as Not enabled in a browser.

claims.claim: No role specifically required to configure the redesigned sharing panel is published in the sources found.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams redesigned in meeting sharing panel license licensing pricing meter prerequisites administrator role. Opened content-sharing policies and the adoption guide page; read MC1317197. No panel-specific configuring role found; tenant disabling is unavailable.

claims.claim: No additional prerequisites specific to the redesigned sharing panel are published in the sources found.
claims.quote: Searched: "new sharing panel" "Teams" license pricing prerequisites admin. Opened content-sharing policies, Teams add-on licenses and the adoption guide page; read MC1317197. No additional panel-specific prerequisite found beyond the notice's stated user/platform scope.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Microsoft has not said how the panel rolls out, so administrators should prepare ahead of the January CY2027 target.
claims.quote: General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-October 2026 (previously late September) and expect to complete by late October 2026 (previously late September).
claims.fix: Retain January CY2027 only as the roadmap target and report the different supplied notice schedule. MC1317197 says Targeted Release meeting controls late July to mid-August 2026, sharing controls beginning September 2026; Worldwide GA mid-October to late October 2026; GCC/GCC High GA late October to mid-December 2026; DoD GA mid-December 2026 to early January 2027. These are Microsoft's announced windows, not verified completion dates. At the 16 November run date, advise checking current tenant rollout and communicating now rather than assuming rollout is entirely ahead. Cite MC1317197 at https://admin.microsoft.com/Adminportal/Home#/MessageCenter/:/messages/MC1317197.

claims.claim: Targeted Release precedes General Availability for this update.
claims.quote: Redesigned Sharing controls will begin rolling out in September 2026. ... General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-October 2026
claims.fix: Attribute the release order to MC1317197 and add its source URL, rather than claiming that the roadmap's unordered phase list establishes the sequence.

claims.claim: Whether an administrator can turn the new sharing panel off at tenant level is an unanswered question.
claims.quote: The new experience is enabled by default and cannot be disabled at the tenant level.
claims.fix: Replace this open question with the notice's distinction: individual users can temporarily return to the previous experience through Teams settings during rollout, but administrators cannot manage that opt-out tenant-wide. Microsoft says the temporary toggle will be retired with advance notice in a separate Message Center post; do not imply permanent retention of the old layout.

claims.claim: Existing content-sharing policy settings govern how users present screens or applications in meetings.

claims.quote: Searched: Teams new sharing panel meeting controls experience licensing default enabled tenant disable MC1317197; Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy ScreenSharingMode parameter. Read content-sharing policies and MC1317197; its policy assurance concerns meeting app pinning, not screen sharing.

claims.claim: Sharing is the most used meeting action.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams sharing most used meeting action screen share telemetry. Checked returned Learn result titles and the cited content-sharing article; read the roadmap and MC1317197. None establishes that sharing is the most used meeting action.
claims.fix: Replace "a different layout for the most used meeting action" with "a different layout for sharing content in meetings".

claims.claim: Microsoft has documented no administrator action for this update.
claims.quote: No immediate action is required. We recommend that you: - Review existing Teams meeting app pinning policies and plan future policies around the two-app limit.
claims.fix: Distinguish no immediate required action from published recommendations. Say Microsoft recommends communicating the redesigned controls and share panel and updating internal documentation and training; its coordinated meeting-controls notice also recommends reviewing app pinning policies against the two-app limit. Cite MC1317197 rather than saying no admin action is documented.
